content.title: About
content.content: The egg sandwich on a bagel is a quick and satisfying breakfast or snack. A round boiled‑or‑baked bagel is topped with a fried or hard‑boiled egg, often accompanied by cheese, ham, lettuce, and a sauce. The combination of a soft bagel, creamy egg, and flavorful add‑ins makes it a favorite in cafés and take‑away spots.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bagels are boiled before baking, giving them a dense, chewy texture.
Eggs are one of the most affordable complete protein sources, containing all essential amino acids.
Egg sandwiches are a staple in American diners and are gaining popularity worldwide.
Variations may include avocado, tomato, spinach, or hummus for extra flavor and nutrition.
Traditional bagels are made from wheat flour, but whole‑grain and gluten‑free versions are widely available.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide complete protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin, and folate, which aid energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in eggs contributes to bone health and immune function.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Adding avocado or a drizzle of olive oil supplies monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Fiber from the bagel
items.content: Whole‑grain bagels add dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from mild to severe.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor intake.

items.title: Sodium in bagels
items.content: Bagels are often salted; low‑sodium options are advisable for those with hypertension.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor salmonella; cook eggs until fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, splitting the bagel in half. Enhance it with fresh veggies, mustard, or a yogurt‑based dip. For a lighter version, choose a whole‑grain bagel and swap cheese for low‑fat cottage cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in plastic wrap. Bagels keep dry in an airtight container for up to 5 days, and hard‑boiled eggs stay safe in the fridge for up to 4 days.
